A `question_log.json` entry, and `ACTIONS.json` entries for the new verbs — transcribed
from the seam after it exists, never authored ahead of it (BL-270 discipline).

items.title: Rivals need to score a stance change as an ordinary candidate
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-17. The reasoning half of the friend/neutral/hostile model - rivals choosing stance on the existing deterministic scored-utility layer, with no new planner and no nation behaviour.
items.design:
## The constraint first

This is a widening of the BL-202/BL-203 exception in exactly the way BL-324 (rival hiring)
was: one more legal verb family on the same deterministic scored-utility layer. It is
**not** a diplomacy planner, has no negotiation state machine, and adds no nation
behaviour — nation actors stay deferred, and stance is corp-to-corp only.

Every term below must be pure, seeded and replayable, computed from world state a rival
can legitimately see under BL-068.

## The scoring terms

**Toward hostile.** Score rises with contested overlap — shared bodies, shared market
bodies, competition for the same scarce resource — and with the relative-strength read
`compute_corp_standings` already produces. It falls with the target military capacity and
with the fraction of the scorer own income that flows through markets the target also
sells into. A corp does not open a war it is losing, and does not burn a market it eats from.

**Toward friendly.** Score rises with complementarity: the target sells what this corp
buys, and their build focuses do not collide. This is where BL-446 (scorer procurement)
composes — a supplier you have completed contracts with is the natural friend, and
`corp_reputation` is already the scalar that says so.

**Toward neutral.** The de-escalation term, and the one most likely to be forgotten.
Without it stances ratchet and every long game ends with everyone hostile to everyone.

## Hysteresis is required, not optional

Stance changes must carry a margin the way the workforce and recipe dials do. A stance
that flips on a marginal score is worse than no stance model, because it makes the
Decision Feed unreadable and makes any downstream military trigger fire on noise. One
stance command per corp per evaluation, and a cooldown before the same pair may move again.

## Legibility

New `corp_decision_reason` values so the Decision Feed reads *why* a rival declared. This
is the item main payoff under spectate: a spectated war whose cause is invisible is a
fight, not a story.

## APPEND-ONLY CONTENTION — recorded 2026-08-22 by the hotspot audit

This item appends to **`corp_decision_reason`** (`src/world/corp_command.hpp`), and so do: BL-446 (procurement), BL-447 (demolish/road).

The enum is **serialised** and append-only: a value may be appended, never inserted or renumbered.
That is a **real ordering constraint between items that share no line of code**, which is exactly
what a file-collision map cannot see — and the backlog recorded it nowhere before now.

**Second-order, and easier to miss:** `corp_decision_reason_count` sizes two FIXED-SIZE ARRAYS in
UI code — `src/ui/strategy_readout.hpp`:64 and a filter loop in the decision feed. An append is
therefore not confined to the world layer, and any item appending here **under-declares its scope**
if it names only `corp_ai.cpp`.

**The batching rule that follows:** one appender per batch, in a stated order, exactly as the
Fall-arc convention already requires elsewhere.

items.title: The spectator harness cannot see a verb the scorer never emits
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-17 from the Sprint 22 audit. spectator_determinism buckets the 15 verbs into four families (build / dial / survey / trade / other), so seven verbs no scorer emits are absorbed silently by families their siblings satisfy.
items.design:
## The blind spot

`family_of()` maps `place_sell_order`, `remove_sell_order`, `request_quote`,
`accept_quote` and `cancel_contract` all to `verb_family::trade`. A rollout in which
rivals place sell orders and do nothing else satisfies the trade family completely, and
the four unemitted verbs beside it are invisible. The same absorption hides `demolish` and
`place_road` inside `other`, which `hire_unit` satisfies on its own.

So the harness that exists to prove spectate exercises the seam proves it at a granularity
too coarse to notice that seven of fifteen verbs never fire.

## Shape

Keep the family assertion — it is doing a different job (BL-409 R1, that no single corp
needs all four families over a short run). **Add** a per-verb histogram over the rollout,
printed always and asserted never. A printed count is the right instrument here: asserting
a floor per verb would fail legitimately whenever a verb is correctly rare, and a harness
that fails legitimately is a harness that gets muted.

The histogram is then the behavioural half of BL-444 (verb coverage tool) static read —
one says the path exists, the other says it was walked.

## Cheap and independent

One file, no world change, no golden movement. It should run first in any reachability
work, because it is the measurement everything else is judged against.

items.title: The convoy layer is the largest built subsystem with no player verb at all
In-flight convoys are drawn on three canvases and listed nowhere
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-17 from the Sprint 25 logistics audit, and filed separately from BL-452 on purpose. Convoys render well - a moving beam with a trailing tail on the Planetary canvas, inter-body lines on the Solar canvas, a convoy glyph under the Supply lens, an aggregated trade-route graph under Supply-routes. What no surface gives is the list: what is in flight, carrying what, from where to where, arriving when, and at what haul cost. A player can watch a convoy and cannot read one.
items.design:
## Why separate from BL-452

BL-350 (procurement seam) landed complete world state, serialisation, validation and a
harness with **no player surface at all**, and nobody noticed for weeks - Sprint 22's
audit found it. A surface that is a task inside the model item is the first thing cut
under pressure. So the press is its own item, blocked on the seam, and the two are
argued against the same behaviour.

## The surface

A **Convoys tab on the Market Ledger**, beside Sell Orders and (per Sprint 22's BL-445)
Contracts. Same chrome, same toggle rule, no new ledger slot on the nav rail.

One row per in-flight convoy of the player's corp: cargo resource and quantity, source
and destination market, mode glyph (land / sea / space - air is never dispatched), a
progress bar off `convoy_component::progress`, **ticks to arrival** derived from
`speed`, and the haul cost already paid. Selecting a row focuses the lane on the active
canvas; the Hold press (BL-452's second verb) sits on the row.

The dispatch press itself belongs on the **market Selection card**, not here - a
dispatch starts from a source you are looking at, and the ledger is the register of what
is already moving.

## The number worth showing that nothing shows today

`ticks to arrival`. The travel-time model landed 2026-08-12 and is genuinely load-bearing
- a long haul now takes several quarters where it used to take one - and **no surface
reports it**. A player who cannot see arrival time cannot feel the change the model made,
which makes it the strongest single argument for this tab.

## Question log

Required, per BL-260: the question is *"what is on its way to me, and when does it land"*.
Drafted rather than settled - Ben's wording.

> ⟳ 2026-08-19 (N1 audit): Re-labelled: LANDED, AWAITING VERIFICATION (bd71143) — not open, do not re-build. Compile-by-inspection favourable (every field read exists in components.hpp:674-705). To close: integrating build (MSVC 14.44), a scripts/verify/convoys.lua (NEW check — naming it in verifier-visual needs Ben's permission; can run as a one-off), the live Hold press per the 2026-08-19 rule, and NR-323's question_log wording once seen. R7 (spectator byte-identity golden) is a SEPARATE pre-existing Windows re-bless owed by the whole Sprint 25a batch — do not conflate.

items.title: An army is bought once and then is free forever - w.units appears in no economic flow
military_points is deleted and science is wired to the tech gate - two write-only accumulators, resolved differently
The military layer has no authority doc, so eleven items point at the AI doc or at nothing
The militia has no military good to buy - ordnance does not exist in the roster
A convoy cannot be intercepted - the logistics network is invulnerable to force
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-17 on Ben's rescope steer. Nothing in the game can stop a convoy. Cargo moves from dispatch to arrival with no interaction with units, stance, terrain control or force of any kind - the logistics layer and the military layer share a world and touch nowhere. This is the item that makes supply lines a military object, and it is the reason BL-454 (upkeep) matters: an army that draws on the network gives an enemy something to cut. SETTLED 2026-08-17 (Ben, on NR-310): cargo is CAPTURED - credited to the interceptor's pool at the interception body - with destruction as the fallback when it cannot be credited.
items.design:
## Why this is the payoff item and not a nice-to-have

BL-454 makes an army draw goods along the network. BL-452 lets a player direct a convoy down
a lane they chose. Neither means anything against an opponent until the lane can be **cut** -
without that, logistics is a cost model and the military layer is a separate game played on
the same map.

It also gives BL-315's own ruling its mechanic. That item settled that **army, mercenary and
pirate are three derived readings of one company** - *the reading is derived, never authored*.
Army and mercenary have paths to being read (BL-377's contracts, a hostile stance). **Pirate
has no mechanic at all**: there is nothing in the game a company can do that would make
"pirate" the honest reading of it. Interdicting a convoy is exactly that act. The naming rule
has been waiting since 2026-08-07 for the verb that earns the third reading.

## The finding that makes this cheap: a convoy already has a position

`convoy_component` stores no path and no tile, which reads at first like interdiction needing
new state. It does not. `body_surface_canvas.cpp` already derives the full tile path per
convoy from `source_market` -> `centre_tile`, `dest_market` -> `centre_tile` and
`intra_body_path`, then interpolates a head along it by `progress`. That derivation is
**deterministic, already cached, and already correct** - it is how the beam renders.

So the work is to move it out of the renderer:

```
entity_id convoy_tile_at(const world& w, const convoy_component& cv);
```

in `logistics.hpp`, returning the tile the convoy's head occupies (or `null_entity` for an
inter-body leg in transit). The canvas then **consumes** the shared function instead of
owning a private copy - which also removes a live duplication, since the renderer's version
would otherwise drift from the world's.

Caution: the canvas copies and conditionally reverses the cached path (`if (st != std::min(st,
dt)) std::reverse(...)`) because `intra_body_path` caches on a canonicalised key. The shared
function must own that orientation rule, or a convoy's head lands at the wrong end of the
lane half the time - a bug that would be invisible on screen (the beam looks fine either way)
and fatal to interdiction.

## Shape

**The trigger.** In the economy tick, after `advance_convoys` and before
`credit_arrived_convoys`: for each convoy, resolve `convoy_tile_at`; if that tile carries a
unit whose owner is **hostile to the convoy's corp** under BL-448's stance table, the convoy
is intercepted. Deterministic, sorted iteration, no RNG in the detection - the roll, if any,
belongs in the resolver, not the trigger.

**Not a battle by default.** A convoy is cargo, not a force. The first cut resolves an
interception as an *outcome*, not as a round-by-round engagement: unescorted cargo meeting a
hostile unit is taken or destroyed. Escort - a unit assigned to a convoy, turning interception
into a real `resolve_campaign_battle` call - is the obvious follow-on and is deliberately not
in this item. It needs BL-315's engagement machinery to be *shipped* rather than merely built.

**Stance is the predicate and the only predicate.** No incidental interception by neutrals, no
terrain-based blockade, no ambient banditry. Hostility is a declared state a corp opts into
(Ben, 2026-08-17, the BL-448 ruling) and interception is one of the things it then permits -
which is also what stops this from being a random tax on trade.

## SETTLED 2026-08-17 (Ben, on NR-310): CAPTURE, with destruction as the fallback

Cargo leaves the source pool at dispatch (SUPPLY.md § Convoy entity), so the goods are
already committed and either answer conserves. Ben chose capture.

**The rule.** On interception the cargo credits the interceptor's `(corp, body)` pool at
the interception tile's body. If it cannot be credited — no pool reachable at that body —
it is destroyed instead, and the outcome says which happened. An interceptor with no market
access holds goods it cannot sell, and that is a legitimate outcome that is **not**
special-cased away.

**Why it matters beyond flavour.** The corp AI is a deterministic scored-utility layer that
prices candidates by payoff. Destroy-only gives an interception a payoff of zero to the
interceptor and a cost in exposure, so BL-450's stance scorer would correctly never rank it
— interdiction would ship and only ever fire when the *player* did it, which is the same
unreachable-capability defect this whole sprint exists to fix. Capture gives the scorer a
number.

**And it earns BL-315's third name.** That item settled that army, mercenary and pirate are
three derived readings of one company, *derived and never authored*. A company that takes
cargo reads as a pirate. One that only burns it reads closer to a saboteur.

**The conservation assertion follows from this and is the harness's load-bearing row:**
captured quantity in == quantity credited, exactly, with the destroyed-fallback path
asserting zero credited and zero minted. No path may create goods.

## Surfaces

An interception is the single most consequential thing that can happen to a player's economy
without them pressing anything, so it cannot be silent: a comms-dock message naming the lane,
the cargo and the interceptor, the convoy's row leaving BL-453's Convoys tab with a stated
cause rather than vanishing, and the interception tile marked on the canvas for a few ticks.
A `question_log.json` entry per surface, per BL-260.

## The check

An `interdiction` harness: (1) `convoy_tile_at` agrees with the renderer's derivation on every
lane in a generated world, in both key orientations - the orientation bug above is the one this
item is most likely to ship; (2) a hostile unit on the head tile intercepts and a neutral one
does not; (3) goods are conserved exactly under capture and exactly destroyed under destroy -
no minting either way; (4) two runs of one seed intercept the same convoys on the same ticks;
(5) an interception with no stance table entry never fires.

## Sequencing - this item is gated and says so

`requires` BL-315 (units must be commandable and standing somewhere on purpose), BL-448 (stance
is the predicate) and BL-452 (a player-directed convoy is the thing worth cutting; auto-dispatch
alone makes interdiction happen *to* the player with no counterplay). **It cannot start before
Sprints 21 and 23 land.** That is the cost of the rescope and it is stated rather than hidden.
items.landed_note: LANDED 2026-08-21, NOT COMPLETE. The mechanic works and is proved (interdiction_harness 49/49 under MSVC, including a mutation check on the path-orientation rule). But it SHIPPED SILENT: the comms message, the Convoys-tab cause and the canvas mark are all absent, because they need an interception_record on world and other lanes held that file. A convoy currently vanishes with no explanation, which the item explicitly says it must not do. See NR-407.

items.title: unit_component::strength duplicates count, and nothing converts a unit into an army_stack_entry
Ordnance cannot be produced at the shipped epoch - the only military good is masked out by its own era tag
The campaign roster band is hard-coded to industrial in a 0 CE product
Every Era -1 harness measures a 4000-year six-band run; generation ships a 400-year one-band run
items.summary: Found 2026-08-18 when Sprint 27's BL-384 agent and Sprint 26b's doc agent reported contradictory facts, and both turned out to be right. history_sim_params defaults to 4000 BCE -> 0 CE across a six-band clock costing 136 decision rounds (history_sim.hpp:126-140). Production overrides all of it: hard_coded_world.cpp:531-536 sets start_year = epoch_year - prehistory_years (0 - 400 = -400), tick_bands[0] = {epoch_year, 4}, tick_band_count = 1 — a 400-year run on one 4-year band, 100 rounds. Every harness takes the struct default, so no check in the project measures the run that actually generates a world.
items.design:
## The divergence, verified

| | span | clock | decision rounds |
|---|---|---|---|
| `history_sim_params` default (every harness) | 4000 BCE → 0 CE | six bands, 100→50→20→10→5→1 | **136** |
| Production (`hard_coded_world.cpp:531-536`) | 400 BCE → 0 CE | one band, 4 years | **100** |

A **10× difference in span** and a different clock shape. `history_sim_harness`, `history_sweep` and the Ages view all read the struct default; only `make_hard_coded_world` overrides it.

## Why this is priority A

**It silently invalidates the instruments the whole Era −1 arc is about to be steered by.** Sprint 27 committed a red conquest assertion measured on the 4000-year ladder. Its findings — the bimodal fight/no-fight split, the Settle-vs-Campaign pricing gap, and the elimination arithmetic — are all measured against a configuration that does not ship.

This is the third instance of this repo's recorded failure mode: Sprint 18 found a visual check pointed at a deleted tab; Sprint 18b found `player_seed_sweep` timing out and never once passing. Both were *checks that looked like coverage and were not*. This is the same shape at the config layer, and it is larger, because it affects **every** Era −1 check at once.

## The consequence that matters most

The BL-384 agent's H2 argues elimination is **arithmetically** unreachable: one verb per polity per round × 136 rounds caps whole-era conquest at 136 provinces, against powers holding ~119–180. **Production has 100 rounds, not 136** — so the ceiling is *tighter* in the shipped world, and the argument gets stronger rather than weaker. But the province counts under a 400-year settlement pass are unmeasured, so the ratio is unknown. **Measure it on the production config before Sprint 28 or Sprint 30 tunes anything.**

## The call this needs (NR-334)

Ben ruled on 2026-08-18 (ruling 8 of NR-331) that the docs were wrong and the **code** was right — keep 400. That ruling was taken against the *production* number, before this divergence was known. The second half is still open: does the **harness** follow production down to 400/one-band, or does **production** follow the struct default up to 4000/six-band? The struct's own comment attributes the six-band ladder to Ben, 2026-08-12, so this is not a stale default — it is a second live intent.

## The work, once the call is made

1. One shared helper that builds the production `history_sim_params`, called by `make_hard_coded_world` **and** by every harness — so the two cannot drift again.
2. Re-run Sprint 27's B384 group on the production config and re-state its findings against it.
3. If both configurations are deliberately kept, every Era −1 harness row must **name which config it measures** in its own output line.

---

> ⟳ **2026-08-23 — FOUR MORE DIVERGENCES, and an exact acceptance test.** BL-554 was filed as a
> separate item and is retired into this one: the adversarial pass over Sprint 28 lane A re-found
> this defect from the other end, in `tools/verify/history_conquest_gap.cpp`, and turned up four
> divergences beyond the span and the clock. **Six in total**, all confirmed in source:
>
> | | app (`hard_coded_world.cpp:536-570`) | harness (`history_conquest_gap.cpp:276-279`) |
> |---|---|---|
> | span | 400 years | **4000** |
> | tick bands | 1, step 4 | **6** |
> | seed | `params.seed ^ 0x415C1E17u` | **bare `wp.seed`** |
> | creeds | `&kepler_creeds` | **`nullptr`** |
> | works | `works` (BL-321's table) | **omitted** |
> | settlement | `kepler_settlement`, pre-sim | **`k->settlement`, POST-sim** |
>
> **Two of the four are structural, not tuning.** `history_sim.cpp:896` gates `build_work` on
> `works != nullptr && works->size() > 0`, so **the harness's verb contest is over four verbs where
> the app's is over five** — and verb competition is precisely what Sprint 28 used this instrument to
> measure. And `k->settlement` is the sim's *output*: `hard_coded_world.cpp:565` mutates
> `kepler_settlement` in place and `:699` copies the result, so the harness runs another 4000 years
> on a world that has already lived through its Era −1.
>
> **The acceptance test is exact and self-verifying**, which this item did not previously have.
> `generation_report::prehistory_battles` / `_conquests` / `_foundings`
> (`hard_coded_world.hpp:379-381`) are written from the app's own run at `:589-590`. So: *for every
> swept seed, a harness's re-run must produce those three numbers bit-equal.* If it does, the harness
> is measuring the app's sim; if it does not, nothing else it prints means anything.
>
> **The fix shape follows from the failure mode.** Copying the app's settings into each harness
> re-creates the defect the next time either moves — the params, the seed derivation and the creed
> derivation should be **one shared call site** both use.
>
> **What this invalidated, now measured.** Seed 0's *generated* era fights 8 battles and takes 8
> conquests; the harness reports zero on the same seed. So Sprint 28's silent-world set and rate are
> both wrong, on top of BL-384's premise and the conquest rate that refuted it. Sprint 28's one
> durable finding — *wherever a world fights nothing, the campaign score clears its threshold and
> loses the argmax on every round*, confirmed at n=32 — is a statement about the decision rule rather
> than about a world, so it is the one thing likely to survive re-measurement. Whether it does is the
> first question this item should answer.

---

> ⟳ **2026-08-23 — FIVE OF THE SIX CLOSED, and the era re-measured.** `src/world/era_minus_one.{hpp,cpp}`
> is the shared call site: it derives the enable gate, the params and the seed, and
> `hard_coded_world.cpp` captures the sim's own arguments through a new optional out-parameter.
> Copying the app's settings into each harness would have re-created this defect the next time
> either moved; both sides now read one function and **cannot** drift.
>
> **The acceptance test passes on 32 of 32 seeds** — the harness's traced re-run reproduces

> **What the corrected fixture says**, and it moves every number the old one produced:
> * **11 of 32 worlds fight nothing (34%)** — not 2 of 8, not 17 of 32.
> * **This item's own premise about BL-384 is now settled**: 2,503 battles produce **1,789
>   conquests (71.5%)**, and no seed fights and takes nothing. *"267 battles, 0 conquests"* was a

> * **Sprint 28's fork answer survives** — all 11 silent worlds read *clears and loses every round*.
>   It transferred because it is a claim about the decision rule, not about a world.
> * **Nothing separates silent worlds from fighting ones.** Ceiling-vs-floor: **32 of 32 overlap**,
>   none disjoint. Score level: silent ceilings 275–439 (median 348) against fighting 350–531
>   (median 405), with 15 of 21 fighting seeds inside the silent range — a shift, not a separation.

items.title: Every world has exactly 31 population centres, and two thirds of nations contain none
Logistic Points - a throughput currency the transport network generates and both goods and force spend
items.summary: Ben, 2026-08-18: "Let's begin codifying Logistic Points in this sprint. It's an important layer for military and goods transport." The concept does not exist anywhere in Io today - no doc, no code, no prior item. This item opens it as DESIGN work inside Lane C1 rather than a build, because its shape has four materially different readings and picking one silently would be the expensive mistake. RULED 2026-08-20 (NR-343): LP is a per-tick RATE - a regenerated throughput allowance, used or wasted each tick, never banked; only the goods it moved carry over. The earlier settled prose recording LP as a stock is superseded by this dated ruling.
items.design:
## What this overturns, stated rather than hidden

`docs/economy/SUPPLY.md` § Infrastructure gates lists **per-node throughput capacity** as *out of prototype scope*, and Sprint 25's block re-affirmed it in its own exclusion list (NR-312). Ben's 2026-08-18 instruction overturns that. Under DELIVERY.md's newest-dated-wins rule this is legitimate; it is recorded here so the reversal is traceable and SUPPLY.md is corrected as part of landing the work, not before it.

## Why the shape is right, independent of the details

**BL-325 ruling 3: one reach field — economic reach IS military reach.** Logistic Points make that ruling *quantitative* rather than merely topological. Today the network answers "can this be reached"; LP would let it answer "how much can move, and what else does that displace". That is the same single network serving goods and force, which is the ruling exactly.

It also gives four already-shipped systems a consumer they lack: road tiers currently only discount cost (`1/(1+0.5*tier)`), ports have no throughput meaning, the Reach lens shows a binary field, and convoys queue without contention.

## The trap this item exists to avoid

**`military_points` was deleted on 2026-08-17 (BL-455) for being a write-only accumulator**, and NR-257 deleted five resources for the same reason a day earlier. A Logistic Point that is generated and never spent — or spent and never felt — is the identical defect with a new name.

**Non-negotiable: LP lands with its consumer in the same batch.** No accrual-only first cut.

## The four readings, which are NOT interchangeable

| | Reading | Generated by | Spent by | Grain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| a | **Per-node capacity** | a node's tier/size | convoys passing through it | node |
| b | **Per-nation budget pool** | the nation's infrastructure | every movement inside it | nation |
| c | **Per-corp allowance** | the corp's own assets | that corp's convoys and units | corp |
| d | **Shadow-Empire style** | infrastructure, as a stock | supply *and* unit upkeep, with distance as the multiplier | mixed |

(d) is the reference Ben's other generation steers point at (PLANETOLOGY.md models the planet pass on Shadow Empire explicitly), and it is the reading in which LP most directly couples military to goods — which is the stated reason for wanting it. It is also the largest.

**Open, and owed to Ben before any code:** which reading; whether LP is a *stock* that accumulates or a *rate* refreshed each tick; whether an over-subscribed network fails, queues, or degrades; and whether the player sees LP as a number, a lens, or only as a refusal.

## Determinism

Whatever the reading, allocation under contention must be **order-independent** — a deterministic priority rule over a sorted set, never first-come by iteration order. `world::state_hash` and the convoy determinism check (`convoy_command.cpp` R5) are the guards.

## Sequencing note

Filed `requires: BL-448` (stance) only because it is promoted inside Lane C1 and shares that sprint's design attention — **not** a code dependency. If interdiction (BL-458) later reads LP, that coupling is filed there, not here.

---

## SETTLED 2026-08-18 (Ben): reading (d) — the Shadow Empire model

*"I'm thinking we can lean heavily on the shadow empire system, and change things if a strong need arrives."*

That closes the four-way fork above. LP is a **stock** generated by infrastructure and spent by both goods movement and unit supply, with **distance as the multiplier** — the reading in which military and economic transport draw on one pool, which is the whole reason Ben asked for it.

**"Change things if a strong need arrives"** is the licence, and it is narrower than it sounds: adapt where Io lacks a Shadow Empire prerequisite, not where the mechanic is merely inconvenient. Every substitution gets written down with the reason, so a later reader can tell an adaptation from a drift.

**The naming rule still binds.** Shadow Empire is a *mechanism* reference exactly as Rome is in HISTORY.md — no term, label or proper noun crosses into Io. "Logistic Points" is Ben's own phrasing and is fine; nothing else transfers by default.

**What this does NOT settle**, and is owed before code: what generates LP and at what rate, the exact consumer that lands in the same batch, the order-independent allocation rule under contention, whether LP enters `world::state_hash` (convoys deliberately do not), and the smallest honest first cut.

---

## CORRECTION 2026-08-18: LP is a RATE, not a stock

The ruling above records LP as *"a **stock** generated by infrastructure"*. **That is wrong about Shadow Empire, and the correction is fidelity to Ben's instruction rather than a departure from it.**

In Shadow Empire, LP is a **per-turn throughput allowance**. Capacity is regenerated each turn by the network and is then used or wasted; what carries over is the resource *stock* it moved, never the points. LP is the pipe; the tanks are separate.

Three consequences, all in Io's favour:

- A rate **crosses no tick boundary**, so it needs no `state_hash` entry and no serialisation — and Io has no save/load layer to add one to.
- A stock that accumulates while never binding is the `military_points` failure with extra steps.
- It removes the largest open question about where LP lives between ticks, because it does not live between ticks.

**Caveat, flagged rather than buried:** this claim comes from Shadow Empire guides, not from anything in this repo. It is the one load-bearing assertion here with no `file:line`, and Ben should confirm it before it hardens.

**CONFIRMED 2026-08-20 (Ben, NR-343 resolved):** LP is a per-tick RATE - regenerated throughput, used or wasted, never banked; the goods it moved are what carry over. The caveat above is discharged; the rate reading is settled.

## Io already owns Shadow Empire's OTHER half, twice over

SE runs **two** currencies: LP (*how much*) from nodes, and Logistical AP (*how far*) from links, where infrastructure quality buys **distance, never capacity**.

Io has the AP half already. `road_traversal_multiplier` = `1/(1+0.5*tier)` is AP-per-hex under another name (`logistics.cpp:62-66`), and `body_reach_field` is SE's free-AP envelope expressed as a cost field.

**So adopt SE's node half and refuse its link half.** Importing AP would be a second parallel distance budget, which BL-325 ruling 3 (one reach field) forbids outright.

## LP is a CAP, not a price

Io's convoy **already charges distance, in credits** — `unit_cost * dist * qty * (1 - node_discount)` (`supply_system.cpp:371`) — and Shadow Empire charges no money for haulage at all.

Adding LP as a second *price* would double-charge distance and move every economy golden. **Credits stay the price; LP decides whether the leg is admissible at all.**

## THE FIRST CUT AS DRAFTED IS REJECTED — two adversarial passes, both structural

Recorded so the next attempt does not re-run into them:

1. **The inertness proof is unachievable as sequenced.** Two-pass allocation reorders float subtractions on a hashed field (`corp.balance -= leg.cost`, `supply_system.cpp:399`), so a "rate-zero, byte-identical" commit cannot pass *at any rate*. The proof pattern BL-409 and BL-454 used does not transfer here, and pretending it does is how a golden gets blessed dishonestly.
2. **LP as drafted has no spatial locus.** § 1 justifies it as *"how much can move through HERE"* — a node — then pools generation per `(corp, body)`. That is not throughput; it is a per-corp haul allowance, which is the exact abstraction `military_points` was deleted for.
3. **The LP cost formula is never specified**, yet the allocation sort key is a function of it. If cost is proportional to distance, LP *is* haulage cost again; if flat, the sort degenerates to tiebreaks.
4. **The base allowance would be the whole mechanic.** No corp is seeded an `inland_logistics_hub`, so *"your own nodes decide how much you may move"* is fictional at the shipped generator — nearly every corp would sit at exactly the base allowance.
5. **The AI pays LP and cannot build the generator.** `corp_ai.cpp` has no `port` and no `inland_logistics_hub` build candidate, so the rate would be an asymmetric tax on rivals.
6. **A reserved military share deletes the coupling it exists to create.** Two budgets means guns and butter stop competing, which was the whole point.
7. **`supply_decay_permille` would ship a one-way ratchet** — `supply_recovery_permille` is *also* 0.0, so a unit short for one tick is permanently degraded.

**What survives and should lead the next attempt:** LP as a cap rather than a price; the node half only; the rate reading; two consumers (`commit_convoy` and `run_unit_upkeep`) that both already exist; and the finding that goods-vs-force priority is currently decided **invisibly by tick phase order** — convoys claim before armies on every code path, so "the army goes unsupplied" is an inherited default nobody chose.

## RULED 2026-08-22 (Ben, design register) — LP IS BIFOLD, AND ACTIVE USE COSTS MONEY

Four answers, and the first reshapes the item.

### 1. Cities generate LP — and LP splits into PASSIVE and ACTIVE

Ben: *"Let's go with city generation, but only because cities have to affect automatic trading. LP
should be bifold then, passive and active. Militaries can only use active LP, and what's more, it
should cost actual money to resolve LP usage. This can be in the form of moving units, or supplying
items."*

**This answers finding 4 and finding 2 of the rejected first cut at once.** Finding 4 was that no
corp is seeded a hub, so a node-generated rate would be fictional at the shipped generator. Cities
are generated in the hundreds, so the rate is real from turn one. Finding 2 was that LP had no
spatial locus; a city is one.

**The split, as ruled:**

| | **Passive LP** | **Active LP** |
|---|---|---|
| Serves | automatic trading — the convoy layer that already runs itself | deliberate movement the player or a rival directs |
| Who may draw it | the market's own flow | **militaries only draw ACTIVE** |
| Whose is it | the network's — ambient | **owned**, and therefore not a rival's to use |

Ben on Q4: *"the passive / active split explains how we would be unable to use rival active LP."*
So **active LP is owned and passive LP is ambient**, and that is what stops a corp free-riding on a
rival's throughput. It also removes the asymmetry finding 5 named, since the ambient half serves
everyone equally.

### 2. Active LP usage COSTS CREDITS — and this is not a reversal of "a cap, not a price"

Ben: *"it should cost actual money to resolve LP usage. This can be in the form of moving units, or
supplying items."*

The cap/price split **holds**: LP decides whether a leg is admissible, credits are what it costs.
What changes is **which side of the game pays**. A convoy already pays credits per unit-distance
(`supply_system.cpp`). **A marching unit pays nothing at all today** — it spends march points
against traversal cost and no money changes hands. This ruling closes that: active LP resolution —
moving units, supplying them — carries a credit cost the military half has never had.

So the shape is: **passive LP caps trade, which is already priced. Active LP caps force, which this
ruling now prices.** Read that way it is a widening of the existing rule rather than an exception
to it.

### 3. Over-subscription FAILS, and the player is told why

Ben chose refusal over queueing and degradation. A refused leg is legible and a queued one is not;
the cost is that LP reads as a wall, which is the honest trade.

**This makes surfacing non-optional** — a refusal nobody sees is BL-458's silent interdiction
again, and the same mistake twice would be a pattern rather than an oversight.

### 4. A lens, extending Reach

Ben chose the lens over a bare number. The Reach lens already exists and shows a binary field;
throughput is that field with a magnitude, so this is a small step from something built rather
than a new surface.

### 5. Hubs become buildable by a rival

Add the port / inland-hub build candidate to `corp_ai.cpp` **before LP lands**, which closes
finding 5.

### What is still owed before code

The rates for both halves; which consumer lands first (`commit_convoy` and `run_unit_upkeep`
both exist); the order-independent allocation rule under contention; and the credit cost of active
resolution, which should be argued against BL-543's value anchor rather than guessed.

items.title: A building 40 tiles from its market clears at the same price as one on the market tile
items.summary: Found 2026-08-18 by the research pass that was sent to evaluate Ben's same-province discount. The discount was rejected as a duplicate of convoy haulage cost - but the pass found the REAL hole it was reaching for. Ordinary auto-surplus clearing debits the corp pool and credits income at ref_price with no convoy created and no leg priced (market_clearing.cpp:747-760). So distance INSIDE a market catchment costs nothing at all: a site on the market centre tile and one forty tiles away clear identically.
items.design:
## The defect

`market_clearing.cpp:747-760` — the auto-surplus path debits the corp's pool and credits income at `ref_price`. **No convoy is created and no leg is priced.** Distance within a catchment is therefore free.

That is the honest version of *"locality is not priced"*. Ben reached for it with a same-province discount; this is the same instinct aimed at the actual hole.

## Why it matters beyond realism

It silently flattens every siting decision inside a catchment. A remote deposit and a deposit on the market's doorstep are worth the same, so the map's geography stops paying — which undercuts the placement-suitability surface, the Opportunity lens, and BL-436's (processing underearns extraction) whole margin question.

## Why it needs NO new grouping

This is the finding that killed the province-discount framing. `price_convoy_leg` **already computes exactly this leg**, over the same reach field BL-325 ruling 3 makes canonical. Nothing new has to be invented, partitioned or named.

## Where to charge it

**At the accrual site, never inside `resolve_price`.** The precedent is BL-343's extraction levy: charge where the flow is *accounted*, not where the price is *resolved*, so the market's quote stays one honest number and the order book's total order is untouched.

Charging inside `resolve_price` would make price depend on who is asking, turning one number into a per-pair matrix and breaking the determinism hash with it.

## Open, and owed to Ben

Full leg cost, or a fraction? Full cost makes remote extraction abruptly unprofitable everywhere at once.

**Measure first.** This makes every remote site less profitable simultaneously, and it lands on an economy whose value-add step is already inverted (BL-436) and whose benchmark reads bankrupt. Sequence it *after* BL-443 (debt floor) so the measurement is readable.

items.title: The province becomes real - a seeded 3-5 tile partition of the land, with the battle footprint as its first consumer
A battle becomes a thing in the world - the province engagement envelope, the stepped span, and the withdraw verb

The battle card - the province map in the Selection band, each unit hit by hit, and the priced exit

items.summary: SETTLED 2026-08-19 (Ben, unit-verb elicitation): the unit marker rides with the verbs - marching invisible armies is absurd. Replaces the chevron deleted uncalled in BL-294 with a marker that has earned its place: units now do something. Adds the march target mode, the unit card's March / Halt / Disband presses, and the headless drivers NR-345 demands.
items.design:
## The marker

A unit glyph at the unit's tile (ICONS.md discipline: shape, meaning, usage, colour source
catalogued; identity colours from presentation.hpp). A marching unit shows its heading; a
unit in battle defers to the battle marker (BL-469). BL-294's deletion is the standard to
clear: that chevron drew nothing anyone could act on. This one marks an object with verbs.

## The command surface

- The unit card (Strength / Roster pages exist) gains an Orders page: current order state
  (holding / marching-to with remaining cost / in battle), and the March, Halt, Disband
  presses. Disband confirms (the BL-449 declare_hostile pattern); Halt is plain; March
  enters target mode.
- **March target mode**: the place-road/place-building targeting pattern - click a
  destination tile, escape cancels. The projected path and its tick cost preview on the
  canvas before the click commits, so distance is priced BEFORE the order, not discovered
  after. Toggle rule applies: re-pressing March while armed disarms it.
- The hover card adds the order state line.

## Verify drivers (the NR-345 debt, paid here)

verify.select_unit(id-or-tile) and verify.march_unit(unit, col, row) land with the surface,
so the card, the marker and the target mode are all photographable headless. Without them
every visual requirement on this item is green-but-blind.

## Question-log entries (BL-260, required)

The marker: "Where are my forces, and where are they going?" The Orders page: "What is this
unit doing, and what can I tell it to do?"

items.title: Formations - composite units that march and fight as one, with preset templates keeping the rock-paper-scissors legible
items.summary: Filed 2026-08-19 from Ben's elicitation note: "a structure to manage groups of units that work as one team over a series of regions... beforehand we should just use common groups, such as 1000 infantry split by groups of 200. And 100 tanks + 400 infantry." A formation is a named grouping of units that marches as one and fights as one side, carrying a doctrine row - which finally gives doctrine_row its campaign consumer. Preset templates first, player-authored composition deferred. The template wheel preserves the class matrix's rock-paper-scissors at formation grain.
items.design:
## What a formation is

A world-held grouping: {members: unit ids, template, name}. Members keep their own
unit_component rows - count, type, supply, tile - so nothing about the settled unit model
moves. The formation adds three behaviours:

1. **Marches as one.** One movement order for the group; the formation moves at its slowest
   member's speed (the historical truth - a column is its baggage). Members co-tile with the
   formation's anchor tile in the first cut; spreading members over adjacent tiles is a
   follow-on, not this item.
2. **Fights as one.** In BL-467's envelope, a formation is one side's stack: members'
   unit_to_stack_entry rows plus the TEMPLATE'S doctrine_row. This is the design's quiet
   win: doctrine_row (frontal_bonus, flank_fragility, mountain_penalty, siege_stance) ships
   today as pure data with no campaign consumer - the formation template is that consumer.
3. **Is commanded as one.** form_up {units, template} / disband_formation {formation} as
   corp_verbs on the one seam (the BL-470 ruling). march_unit accepts a formation id where
   it accepts a unit id.

## Ben's examples, read against the model (2026-08-19 note, verbatim anchors)

"1000 infantry split by groups of 200" - a template speaks RATIOS over classes and a
sub-group granularity, not absolute headcounts (hire_batch_manpower is 50 today; the batch
size is data and may move). "100 tanks + 400 infantry" - a 1:4 shock-to-foot combined-arms
mix; in class terms the tank IS the cavalry class's industrial row, so the template is
era-invariant: the same mix is lancers-and-levies at 0 CE and armour-and-rifles at 1960.
Era-invariance of templates matches BL-314's verbs-are-era-invariant ruling exactly.

## The template wheel - keeping rock-paper-scissors legible

The class matrix already runs infantry > ranged > cavalry > infantry. Templates COMPOSE it
rather than replace it, and the wheel must survive at formation grain:

| Template | Mix (by weight) | Doctrine lean | Beats | Loses to | Ground |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Line** | 80 infantry / 20 ranged | frontal_bonus high, flank_fragility high | Screen | Wing | anchored, rough - defence country |
| **Screen** | 60 ranged / 40 infantry | low frontal, low fragility | Wing | Line | forest, highland - cover country |
| **Wing** | 60 cavalry / 20 infantry / 20 ranged | high frontal, mountain_penalty high | Line | Screen | plains - open country |
| **Spearhead** | 20 cavalry / 60 infantry / 20 ranged | moderate everything, low fragility | none hard | none hard | any - the generalist premium |
| **Train** | 30 siege / 50 infantry / 20 ranged | invest stance | (fortifications, future) | everything in the open | roads - it barely moves |

- **Line > Screen > Wing > Line** is the wheel, and it derives from the matrix: a Line's
  infantry mass closes on a Screen's ranged core; a Screen's massed ranged shreds a Wing's
  cavalry; a Wing flanks a Line's fragility. No template beats its counter through raw
  numbers alone at even strength - that is the legibility invariant, and the harness asserts
  it the way combat_harness R3 already asserts doctrine purity.
- **Spearhead is deliberately counter-free both ways** - the combined-arms generalist
  (hammer-and-anvil, armour-plus-infantry). Its edge is flexibility, priced by never having
  a favourable matchup. Ben's tanks+infantry example lands here.
- **Train exists for the future fortification system**; in the open field it is prey, which
  the matrix already encodes (siege uniformly weak). Its escort keeps it from being a free
  kill, no more.
- **Terrain rotates the wheel, it never breaks it**: mountain and forest amplify Line and
  Screen (terrain_defence, doctrine mountain_penalty against the Wing), plains amplify the
  Wing, wetland punishes Wing and Train (attrition 350, the marsh-stops-armies reading).
  All of that is EXISTING numbers - templates add no new terrain table.

## Presets first, customisation deferred - explicitly

The five templates ship as AUTHORED DATA (lua, the params precedent): ratios, sub-group
granularity, doctrine values. Player-authored templates (choose your own mix and doctrine)
are a named follow-on slice, not silently dropped - the note's "this can be customizable"
is the licence, and the deferral is so the wheel is proven legible before it is player-bent.

## Determinism and naming

- form_up validates every member (owned, same tile, not in battle) and mutates nothing on
  rejection. Formation ids are entity ids; iteration follows the sorted-id rule everywhere.
- "Formation" enters GLOSSARY.md with the work (the name-it-first rule). Template display
  names are authored data and must come from the seeded banks if they are ever generated -
  never Earth proper nouns. Line/Screen/Wing/Spearhead/Train above are design labels, not
  shipped strings.

## Open, named

- Per-class march speed (a Wing should outpace a Line) - interacts with slowest-member rule;
  derive any speed from the roster row (NR-322's one-source discipline).
- Whether a formation's members can straddle tiles (frontage on the battle map) - deferred
  with the spreading follow-on.
- Reinforcement: can a unit join a formation mid-campaign at distance, or only co-tile?
  First cut: co-tile only.

## 2026-08-19 - the presets are COMPOSITE UNITS; formations remain above them (Ben's correction)

Ben, review-verdict form: *"I was imagining formation pre-sets as composite units rather
than formations. My bad with the word choice. We can use both though."* So the model gains
a layer and keeps the other - two objects, both real:

- **Composite unit** - ONE unit entity whose composition spans classes: a composition
  vector over {cls -> manpower share}, set by its template at muster. "Muster a Spearhead"
  is a single press at the base: 100 shock + 400 foot arrive as one token, one marker, one
  order, one supply read. The FIVE PRESET TEMPLATES SHIP AT THIS GRAIN (all five confirmed
  this date). unit_to_stack_entry becomes one-to-many - one stack entry per component
  class - and derived strength sums components. The hire gate is the union of every
  component row's gates; the price sums component costs through the existing power-mod
  pricing. It marches at its slowest component's class speed.
- **Formation** - the grouping of units (simple or composite) that marches and fights as
  one, as designed above. This is where customisation and the multi-unit army live -
  "1000 infantry split by groups of 200" is a formation of five infantry units. Doctrine:
  a lone composite unit fights under its own template's doctrine row; a formation's
  template doctrine governs the whole side when grouped.

The wheel analysis is unchanged - it holds at whichever grain instantiates it, because both
resolve to the same class-mix stacks.

items.title: Clicking a tile shows its province - the Selection band renders the locality cell, and the tile preview outlines it

This should also be rendered in the selection tile preview." The province (BL-466, the 3-5 tile locality cell) becomes visible the moment a tile is selected - before any battle exists to draw it.
items.design:
## Shape

- The tile card gains a province read: the selected tile's province, shown as its member
  tiles. Provinces are deliberately nameless (purely spatial, the GLOSSARY ruling), so the
  read is structural - "one of 4 tiles" plus the outline - not a name line.
- **The hex-neighbourhood preview outlines the province**: the member tiles of the selected
  tile's province get a distinct stroke inside the existing preview widget. One visual

## Question-log entry (BL-260, required)

"Which tiles move and fight as one locality with this one?" - the answer surface a player
needs BEFORE committing units, since the envelope decides who is drawn into a fight.

items.title: A Diplomatic lens shows stance geographically, replacing the all-corporations table as BL-449s surface
items.summary: Ben, 2026-08-19: the all-corporations Stance table (BL-449) is too much information at once and not the shape he pictures for this. Redirect: a Diplomatic overlay_mode joining the corporation/country/resource/etc. roster, tinting tiles or corp markers by the players stance toward the owning corp (Hostile/Friend/Neutral/Unknown per NR-350), so relationships read on the map the way ownership and production already do. Supersedes the table-column approach BL-449 shipped and NR-353 found unreachable - that column is retired, not fixed. [PARKED 2026-08-19 (Ben): basic military function (each corp starts with an army) takes priority; diplomacy surfacing is a tangent for now. In-flight WIP (not landed, not verified) sits uncommitted-to-main on branch worktree-agent-a2b81665b3439a110, commit 6ad58a3 - resume from there rather than restarting.]
items.design:
## Why this instead of the table

BL-449 tried to put four extra facts (Reach/Capital/Share/Stance) plus three presses into the all-corporations table already living in the narrow shell fold-out column. NR-353 found the result unreachable in play - the Stance columns buttons render off the panel edge, and BL-111 had already narrowed that same table once before for the identical reason (six columns collapsed to single-glyph headers).

Ben's redirect, 2026-08-19: this is backend-useful information, not player-facing information in that shape. A lens is the existing vocabulary for at-a-glance relational state across many entities at once - Corporation lens already tints tiles by owner, Country lens by nation. Diplomatic stance is the same shape of fact (a per-corp category) and belongs in the same family, not in a giant table.

## Scope (design-owed - settle before promoting)

- Where the tint reads: tile fill (like Corporation lens) vs. a marker/ring on each rivals HQ/buildings (lighter-weight, avoids implying stance is a REGION when it is a relationship between two corps). Lean toward the marker/ring approach given stance is corp-to-corp, not corp-to-territory - but this is the first open question for Ben.
- Colour/glyph vocabulary for Hostile/Friend/Neutral/Unknown - four states need four legible marks, and Unknown (BL-068 gated, NR-350) must read as distinct from Neutral rather than simply absent.
- Bar or off-bar placement (LENSES.md "Bar" column) - stance is not yet consequential (BL-448 lands the substrate inert), so off-bar (like Scarcity/Industry/Reach) may be the honest placement until BL-315/BL-467 give it a gameplay payoff, matching how those lenses graduated onto the bar only once their consequence landed.
- Whether the three transition presses (Declare Hostile / Offer Friendship / Return to Neutral) live in the lens itself (a marker click opens a small popup) or move entirely into the Selection panel (see BL-475) - if the latter, this lens is READ-ONLY and simpler to design.

## What it does not carry

No new data model - BL-448s stance.hpp tables are already correct and load-bearing. This item is purely the map-surface read; BL-475 is the per-corp detail + action surface.

## SETTLED 2026-08-19 (Ben, elicitation form)

- **Tint target: TILE FILL, not the marker/ring recommendation.** A deliberate overrule — Ben wants stance to read as a territory tint like the Corporation lens, not a per-building marker. This makes the corp-vs-territory framing in this item's earlier text moot; the lens colours the rival's owned tiles by the player's stance toward them, same visual family as Corporation/Country.
- **Bar placement: ON THE BAR, not off-bar.** A second deliberate overrule of the "not consequential yet" reasoning — Diplomatic joins Corporation/Country/Resource/etc. as a primary, always-reachable lens from day one rather than waiting for BL-315/BL-467 to give stance a gameplay payoff.
- **Marker click: clicking a tinted tile/rival selects that corp and jumps to its Selection panel** (BL-475) — the lens is a read surface, selection is the existing canvas click-to-select path, no bespoke popup.
- **Presses live ONLY in the Selection panel (BL-475)** — confirmed, matches the recommendation. This lens carries no interactive presses of its own.
- **Colour vocabulary: the recommended scheme, confirmed.** Hostile red, Friend green, Neutral grey, Unknown a dashed/hollow grey ring — Unknown must never read as a blank tile (NR-350).

Both overrules recorded per this project's standing practice of flagging where Ben's choice differs from the filed recommendation and why it matters: tile fill reads Diplomatic as territory-like from the start, and bar placement means it ships visible before it has any gameplay consequence — a deliberate legibility-first call, not an oversight.

items.title: The per-corporation Selection ledger carries stance detail and the three transition presses
items.summary: Ben, 2026-08-19, companion to BL-474: expand the per-corporation Selection ledger to carry stance and any other relevant from-our-perspective detail, replacing the all-corporations tables Stance column as the place the three transition presses (Declare Hostile / Offer Friendship / Return to Neutral) actually live. Selecting a rival corp (from the canvas, a lens marker, or the corporations list) shows the relationship as ONE corps detail, not a row in a giant comparison table. [PARKED 2026-08-19 (Ben): basic military function (each corp starts with an army) takes priority; diplomacy surfacing is a tangent for now. In-flight WIP (not landed, not verified) sits uncommitted-to-main on branch worktree-agent-a2b81665b3439a110, commit 6ad58a3 - resume from there rather than restarting.]
items.design:
## Why the Selection panel, not the table

SELECTION.md already owns the pattern for one-entity detail across the game (Active/Focus/Selection states, shared per-entity content builders the Tile Ledger and hover card also use). Stance-toward-one-corp is exactly that shape of fact - it belongs where a player already looks to learn about ONE thing, not crammed into a table meant to compare MANY things at once (which is what made BL-449s column unreachable, NR-353).

## Scope (design-owed - settle before promoting)

- Where in the Selection cards existing layout the stance block sits, relative to whatever a corp selection already shows (BL-081/BL-214s roll-up cards, per question_log.jsons corporation_dashboard entry).
- The three presses (Declare Hostile with its confirm popup on the demolish precedent, Offer/Accept Friendship, Return to Neutral) move here from the retired table column - same corp_command verbs from BL-448, same rejection handling, same NR-350 visibility gate (do not show anything for an undiscovered corp beyond Unknown).
- Whether BL-474s lens markers are clickable to select-and-jump here, or selection only happens via the existing canvas/list paths - affects whether BL-474 needs any interactivity of its own.

## What it does not carry

No new data model or verbs - BL-448s stance.hpp and its four corp_command verbs are unchanged. This is purely re-hosting an already-correct interaction onto the right surface. ACTIONS.json/question_log.json entries move with it (retitle rather than duplicate - BL-449s existing corporation_panel entries describe the retired surface).

## SETTLED 2026-08-19 (Ben, elicitation form, alongside BL-474)

- **This item now owns ALL three transition presses exclusively** — BL-474's lens is confirmed read-only, so Declare Hostile / Offer Friendship / Return to Neutral live here and nowhere else.
- **Entry point confirmed: selecting a tinted tile/rival under the Diplomatic lens (BL-474) jumps here** — the existing canvas click-to-select path, no new selection mechanism needed.
- Layout position within the existing Selection card stack is still an implementation call for whoever promotes this — not re-elicited, low-stakes relative to the placement/interaction questions above.

items.title: Every corporation starts with an army, not just the player
Each era has a collapse state to avoid — that is what defines meta
items.summary: Ben, 2026-08-19 (version-alignment form, verbatim): "We should have a paradigm that makes nuclear war unlikely, but a clear looming threat for this Era. In general, each era has a 'collapse' state to avoid - and that's what defines meta." The paradigm: every era names ONE collapse state — the ancient era's is imperial collapse (the Fall arc, Sprint 30's strain machinery); the industrial/space era's is the nuclear rupture (BL-333's parked arc, HISTORY.md stage 6). Meta systems (tech BL-479, law BL-480, policy BL-155/BL-156) must couple their levers to the era's collapse pressure — a tech or law is interesting because it moves the world toward or away from the brink, not because it moves a growth curve.
items.design:
## The paradigm

Each era carries one named collapse state the world can fall into, and the meta layer — tech, law, policy — is defined by its relationship to that state. Design-owed: (1) name the ancient era's collapse pressure in ERAS.md terms and wire it to the Fall arc's strain/hegemony machinery (Sprint 30) so campaign-era play inherits a live, legible threat, not lore; (2) specify how the modifier vocabulary (BL-479) expresses collapse-coupled effects — e.g. a law that trades treasury for cohesion, a tech that extends reach at the cost of strain; (3) the nuclear paradigm for the space arc stays parked with BL-333 but this item's framing must not contradict it. RULED (Ben, 2026-08-20): **genuinely reachable.** The collapse state is a real campaign fail-state, not a pressure valve the meta always buys off. Two consequences bind the design: (1) the strain/collapse machinery Lane A builds for the Era −1 sim (Sprint 30) is a SHARED mechanism the campaign inherits, not generation-only plumbing; (2) meta levers (tech BL-479, law BL-480) can move the world toward or away from the brink but must never be able to wall it off entirely — a world played badly enough collapses, and the meta is interesting because the threat is real.

items.title: Research becomes a currency the corp spends
items.summary: Extracted from parked BL-087 (Era-1 tech/quest system) piece 2 on Ben's 2026-08-19 verdict — the accrual/cost/debit mechanism Sprint D2 needs. Fall-arc ruling 6: science is SPENT, not reached. What shipped 2026-08-17 (BL-455) is a LEVEL — condition_subject::science as a threshold; spending needs a debit the level model never had: an accrual (exists), a cost per ladder node, a debit at the moment a node is taken. Loads docs/research/ancient_tech_ladder.json (92 objects) and authors the T1-T2 gates with ENFORCED prerequisites. The condition_set.hpp:70-75 comment block asserting reached-not-spent must be rewritten in the same change (verdict M2) — it is true today and becomes a lie the day this opens.
items.design: Design-owed. Boundary settled 2026-08-19 (verdict M3, Ben's pick): this is the live arc's spend mechanism, extracted from BL-087 piece 2; BL-087's era-event/quest framing stays parked. Sprint D2 is the build home; sequence after BL-479 (the effect union) so a purchased node can express more than a building unlock.

items.title: A tech can express a buff — the effect union and the modifier vocabulary
A law has an author, and a tax is a transfer
items.summary: Sprint D3's build item (Lane D, opened 2026-08-19 in one batch with D1 per Ben's verdict). Three defects, one item: struct law has no author (BL-155: non-deferrable — "a law with no author is not migratable later"); the enacted levy DESTROYS money (debited from the corp, credited to nothing); and enactment is a debug checkbox on the player's balance ledger — a corporation flipping world law. [LANDED 2026-08-19 @ merge c00bba8, awaiting two things: Ben's live look at the read-only levy line (R3 half) and the NR-382 rate ruling — the placeholder 1.0/unit all-resources rate, biting now the law ships enacted, drives every rival insolvent; ai_skill bands left red-and-attributed, deliberately unblessed. Conservation/scope/repeal all green (14/14 + 24/24).]
items.design:
## Shape

1. `struct law` gains `enacting_nation` (entity id) and an applicability scope (the enacting nation's jurisdiction — corps whose taxed flow lands in its territory). A law with no author cannot exist any more.
2. `nation_component` gains a `treasury` (credits). The levy becomes a TRANSFER: debit the payer, credit the enacting nation's treasury, sum conserved — asserted by harness.
3. Enactment moves off the player's ledger. The balance-ledger checkbox (balance_ledger.cpp:277-279) is removed; the seeded law set is enacted at generation by its author nation, deterministically. A nation CHOOSING to enact mid-campaign is the BL-202/BL-203-shaped scored decision the 2026-08-18 nation grant permits — may stub as generation-seeded only this sprint, with the seam shaped for the scorer.
4. The player's laws surface (BL-186, amended today) reads: which laws bind me, whose, what they cost me — browse-only.
5. Wages-above-a-legal-floor: severable; take only if the modifier vocabulary (BL-479) lands first and names wage_floor, else leave to a follow-on.

Guards: harness proves (a) conservation (levy sum debited == treasury sum credited), (b) scope (an out-of-jurisdiction corp pays nothing), (c) repeal returns bit-identical to baseline, (d) no player-reachable enact control remains (the untrusted-boundary rule applies if any seam verb is added — reject, never clamp).

items.title: The blackboard export is 60x too large for a local model — fuse the triples, hoist the envelope
items.summary: BL-335's measurement (2026-08-19): one player blackboard read is ~74 KB / ~18.5K tokens, refreshed every decision because state changes each tick — an 8B local model at 8K context cannot hold ONE export, and at 32K it eats half the window per decision. 96% of the bulk is two families: the market price/demand/supply triple (351 facts, 53%) and the rival-building owner/tile/type triple (258 facts, 43%), each fact repeating a ~70-byte constant envelope (_v, t, confidence, provenance) around ~45 bytes of payload. The word-interface direction (AI_OPPONENT.md § 10, tight-local-model bias) requires the compact encoding this item builds.
items.design:
## Shape

1. FUSE the per-subject triples: one row per (market, resource) carrying price+demand+supply; one row per rival building carrying owner+tile+type. Pure re-encoding, zero information loss — measured to cut the bulk ~3x (to ~25 KB / ~6K tokens); a tabular encoding lands ~12 KB / ~3K tokens.
2. HOIST the constant envelope (_v, t, confidence, provenance) to a stream header; facts carry payload only, with per-fact overrides where a value genuinely differs.
3. FILTER seam (client-side or a query arg): own-assets slice (~3 KB) + market rows for resources the corp holds or can extract. The full export stays available — the compact form is an additional shape, not a replacement, so BL-204's goldens and every existing consumer are untouched.
4. Guard: a harness asserts the fused form round-trips to the same fact set as the verbose form on the canonical world (information-preservation, not golden bytes).

Consumers: BL-306 (client loop) reads it; BL-279's corpus (parked) inherits it for free. Version: v0.1.16 (The watch) — it gates a usable local-model session on the seam BL-412 is landing.

items.title: The Economy panel pools view leaks every corp's stockpiles to a played session
items.summary: Found in passing by the BL-408 god-view build (2026-08-19): economy_panel.cpp draw_pools lists EVERY corp's (corp, body) pool quantities to an ordinary played session — a straight violation of the BL-068 competitor-visibility rule (rival buildings visible, internals private), predating the god-view work entirely. God view now makes this information legitimately visible under spectate; the played-session path must redact rival pools to the same standard the Selection/hover surfaces already meet.
items.design: Gate draw_pools rows on ownership: the player's own pools render as today; rival rows redact quantities (or drop) unless spectating && god_view. Follow the exact test BL-408 planted at its read-sites so the two paths cannot drift. One file, one gate; verify with a played-session capture beside the existing spectator_god_view.lua ON/OFF legs.

items.title: Transformation (E4): the mandate resets the regime, the map holds
items.summary: The dynastic-cycle allegory's exit: strain > cohesion WITH high works/institutions resolves by re-founding, not fragmentation - same borders, new polity, reset strain, partial capacity regression, legitimist creed. The cheapest culmination (no map change) and the one that keeps region counts stable.
items.design: Exit selection is DETERMINED by the state vector at break (COLLAPSE.md open question 2's lean): the works/cohesion-infrastructure level is the discriminant between E4 and E1. The successor keeps the ancestor's name lineage via the phoneme generator's variation path, not a fresh mint.

items.title: Exodus (E5): the rump state and the migration
items.summary: A breaking or absorbed polity with an open frontier survives displaced - Settle fired as a survival verb. Yields a small, high-cohesion survivor far from home with maximal grudge, and frontier regions gaining unearned population/capacity. The map texture Sprint 29 wants: capitals in strange places, with reasons.
items.design: Trigger: E1/E3 resolution where a frontier region within reach is unheld. The chosen-remnant creed locks legitimist + max grudge (COLLAPSE.md pattern library).

items.title: The Slow Fade (E6): senescence below a relevance threshold
items.summary: No rupture: a major chronically NEAR the break, never over it, erodes - piecemeal border recession and a demotion below the hegemony measure. The Metropole's default ending and the sim's best source of interesting small nations at 0 CE: proud creed, high grudges, disproportionate reach.
items.design: Detection: N consecutive years in the top strain band without a break event. Effect: periphery provinces detach singly (to neighbours or owner_none) at a deterministic trickle; the polity survives as a minor.

items.title: Cohesion reads interdependence: the substrate for systemic collapse (E7)
items.summary: The Bronze-Age allegory: one break cascades because neighbours' cohesion rested on the broken polity's trade and tribute. Needs cohesion to carry an interdependence input - a real design decision, deliberately sequenced AFTER E1-E4 land and are measured (COLLAPSE.md's own caution).
items.design: A per-polity term derived from routes/works shared with neighbours; an E1/E3 event that severs them debits the survivors' cohesion. Candidate for a RARE outcome band asserted by sweep, never scripted. The most expensive culmination; hold until the others are measured.

items.title: Seeded polity creeds from the pattern library, biasing the culmination
items.summary: COLLAPSE.md's ideological axis made mechanical: creed is seeded data per polity (mandate / remnant / stewardship / restoration leans from the pattern library), and the state vector that determines the exit includes it - same strain, different story, different ending, deterministically.
items.design: A small enum-weighted axis set written at polity creation and mutated only by culminations. Consumed by: exit determination (E4 vs E1 vs E5), Release scoring (stewardship-lean raises it), and Sprint 29's nation-character payload. This is where 'the story IS the character payload' becomes code.

items.title: The six-strategy roster as seeded weighting profiles over polity verbs
items.summary: Tortoise / Pulse / Hydra / Phoenix / Metropole / Temple as data: per-polity verb-weighting profiles assigned at seed, deterministic, replayable. The tuned-attractors ruling means these are the diversity source the sweep asserts distinctness over - not templates that script outcomes.
items.design: Each profile is a weight vector over {Campaign, Settle, Invest, Consolidate, Release} plus thresholds (Pulse's strain switch, Hydra's release band, Phoenix's neighbour-collapse gate). Profiles live in history params so tuning is a data change. Distinctness asserted by BL-490.

items.title: History-tab narration per culmination and narrative pattern - quiet by design
items.summary: Each culmination emits its narrated line(s) in the history log, minted from the pattern library (the declinist mirror precedes the break; the mandate withdrawn explains E4; the garden given away recasts E2). Ruling 2026-08-20: surfaces in the history tab only - seeing beats telling, deep-dig optional, never chrome pushed at the player.
items.design: Template lines keyed by (culmination, creed) filled with phoneme-generated names. Driven, not narrated: every line is emitted BY an event that occurred. Sibling to BL-300 (myth/theology), which owns the authored bank's voice; a devolution that plays back as silence looks like a bug (COLLAPSE.md open question 4).

items.title: The attractor sweep: four allegory arcs at reported rates, strategies distinct
items.summary: The tuned-attractors ruling's enforcement: across N seeds, assert each allegory arc (fragmentation, devolution, transformation, cascade) occurs at a stated, REPORTED rate - never clamped - and each strategy profile is observably distinct in lifespan, fragment count and successor share. Two indistinguishable strategies mean one is dead weight; a culmination that never fires is scope to cut.
items.design: Extends the existing sweep harness. Rates pinned BEFORE tuning (the adversarial pass's discipline: the number must not be chosen to match the result). The strategy x culmination matrix in COLLAPSE.md is the literal assertion table.

items.title: Event-driven quiet provinces: stable interiors wake on events, not per year
items.summary: Perf rung 2 of COLLAPSE.md's 4000-year ladder. Most of 4000 years, most provinces do nothing; give stable interior provinces a fast path that wakes on border change, strain band crossing, or route loss - never a per-year evaluation.
items.design:
Wake conditions are pure functions of sim state (deterministic; asserted by the prehistory-on determinism case). Converts per-year cost from O(provinces) toward O(changes). Depends on BL-320's spatial index + incremental aggregates landing first (rung 1).

## RE-VERSIONED 2026-08-22 — v0.1.16 → v0.1.19 (Ben's call, on NR-537)

`requires` **BL-320** (Era-1 sim perf), which is **v0.1.19**. This item is the quiet-province fast
path and BL-320 is the perf work it sits on, so v0.1.19 is where both belong.

The rule this applies: **an item cannot be scheduled into a minor its own blockers land after.**
A minor cannot cut while part of it waits on a later one, so the version goal was a scheduling
claim the dependency graph contradicted. Moving the item is the cheaper of the two fixes — the
other is moving three blockers forward, which would drag their own chains with them.

items.title: Deterministic banded year grain: quiet ages step coarse, crises step yearly
items.summary: Perf rung 3. Simulate quiet bands at 5-10 year steps with scaled verb effects; drop to yearly grain when any polity's strain, war state, or culmination proximity crosses a band. Targets the year count directly - the rung that makes 4000 years affordable.
items.design:
The grain switch MUST be a pure function of sim state - seeded, replayable, asserted by the determinism case - or it is a die roll wearing a timestep (COLLAPSE.md's own words). Verb effect scaling at coarse grain must be exact-integer so no drift separates a watched run from a skipped one.

## DEPENDENCY CORRECTED 2026-08-22 (hotspot audit)

`requires` named **BL-491** (quiet-province fast path). Wrong dependency. This item's own design
says the band switch fires *"when any polity's strain, war state, or culmination proximity crosses a
band"* — **that needs strain to exist**, which is BL-504.

The correction matters for scheduling rather than for correctness: BL-491 requires BL-320, a
**v0.1.19** item, so the stale dependency chained a v0.1.16 item behind a minor three later. Against
BL-504 — also v0.1.16 — it is startable inside its own minor.

## DELIBERATELY NOT RE-VERSIONED 2026-08-22

The other three items of the perf chain moved out of v0.1.16 on Ben's call (NR-537). **This one
stayed**, and the reason is recorded so it is not swept along on a later pass.

Its `requires` named **BL-491**, which is a v0.1.19 item — and that dependency was simply **wrong**.
This item's own design says the band switch fires *"when any polity's strain, war state, or
culmination proximity crosses a band"*: that needs **strain**, which is BL-504, a **v0.1.16** item.
Corrected the same day.

So it is startable inside its own minor and there is nothing to move. **BL-494 now depends on it
from v0.1.22, which is the correct direction** — a dependency in an earlier minor is exactly what a
version goal should express.

items.title: Record the run on change, at the reader's grain
items.summary: Perf rung 4 - the recording half, which BL-425 measured as the real hang (>8 min Debug for the per-year time-lapse). Snapshot ownership on owner_changes (already exists) plus per-decade otherwise; narrated lines are events, not per-year state. The history tab scrubs decades in practice.
items.design:
Memoise the record at generation time in BL-427's world-snapshot cache so --verify pays nothing. Un-parks scripts/verify/parked/history_ages.lua as part of landing (BL-425's own close-out).

## RE-VERSIONED 2026-08-22 — v0.1.16 → v0.1.22 (Ben's call, on NR-537)

`requires` **BL-425** (ages lazy sim unaffordable, still `design-owed`) and **BL-427** (verify
world-snapshot cache), **both v0.1.22**. Its sim-side content is only a handful of lines around
`owner_changes` / `out.history`; the weight is in the surfaces those two items own.

The rule this applies: **an item cannot be scheduled into a minor its own blockers land after.**
A minor cannot cut while part of it waits on a later one, so the version goal was a scheduling
claim the dependency graph contradicted. Moving the item is the cheaper of the two fixes — the
other is moving three blockers forward, which would drag their own chains with them.

items.title: Extend the Era -1 run to the 4000-year ladder and re-pin the bands
items.summary: The ruling itself (Ben, 2026-08-20): the 400-year band was a placeholder; the aim is 4000 years so the four allegory arcs chain sequentially per world. Extends prehistory_years and the band ladder; re-pins every generation golden and the BL-224 non-hegemony bands by measurement.
items.design:
Lands LAST in the perf ladder - after BL-320 (rung 1), BL-491 (rung 2), BL-492 (rung 3), BL-493 (rung 4) - and only if the /O2 measurement fits the generation budget; the honest fallback (2-3 completed arcs per world, all four attractors asserted across the sweep) degrades density, never determinism. Reverses the Sprint 26b doc-truth correction knowingly: HISTORY.md's 400-year note gains a dated supersession pointing here.

## RE-VERSIONED 2026-08-22 — v0.1.16 → v0.1.22 (Ben's call, on NR-537)

`requires` **BL-320** (v0.1.19), **BL-491** (now v0.1.19) and **BL-493** (now v0.1.22) — so the
latest blocker sets the floor, and that is v0.1.22. The hotspot audit adds a fourth reason the
backlog did not record: this item cannot ship without **BL-462**'s territory (also v0.1.22), since
BL-462 owns the harness-vs-production config divergence that BL-494 would otherwise have to close
twice.

The audit also found its file scope wrong in a way that matters here: it declares only
`history_sim.{hpp,cpp}` and is **missing `src/world/hard_coded_world.cpp`**, where its entire
deliverable actually lives.

The rule this applies: **an item cannot be scheduled into a minor its own blockers land after.**
A minor cannot cut while part of it waits on a later one, so the version goal was a scheduling
claim the dependency graph contradicted. Moving the item is the cheaper of the two fixes — the
other is moving three blockers forward, which would drag their own chains with them.

items.title: Held convoy cargo stays visible to the price signal
items.summary: Ben's ruling on NR-317 (2026-08-20): a held convoy's cargo counts in the scarcity/price calculation, aligning with BL-422's convention for held sell orders (held stock stays visible so scarcity is not gameable). Closes the parked-outside-the-economy exploit shape without new cost machinery - one convention everywhere.
items.design: Wherever resolve_price / the rarity input aggregates available stock, include cargo aboard held convoys at the destination market's scope, exactly as BL-422 includes held orders. No upkeep charge, no expiry - the hold stays a legitimate strategic pause; only its invisibility goes. Assert with a headless case: holding a convoy moves no price.

items.title: Ordnance upkeep rate leaves zero when battle consumption lands
items.summary: Ben's ruling on NR-321 (2026-08-20): the ordnance (and food_rations) upkeep rates ride Lane C's engagement trigger - the first real draw coincides with combat that spends it, one golden re-bless instead of two.
