**NR-503's overdraw must not come back.** The Country legend used to paint free-hand
on the canvas, bounded to the *canvas* vertical span — which runs behind the bottom
panels — so at 40 nations it **overprinted the tile ledger outright**, and nothing
caught it: `text_overflow_floor` looks for **clipped** text, and this text was not
clipped, it was overdrawn. A legend drawn inside the minimap box must therefore be
**clipped to that box**, so overflow scrolls rather than escapes. Being "inside the
minimap" is a promise only if the clip rect enforces it.

## Sequencing note

**BL-535** retires `overlay_mode::country` outright — which removes the 40-row legend
that motivated BL-533 in the first place, and with it the worst case this item has to
fit. Worth sequencing after it, or at least landing in the knowledge that it is
coming.

items.title: The province is the unit of conquest - a tile cannot change hands without it
items.summary: Ben, 2026-08-22: 'have it be impossible to conquer a tile without also controlling the province'. Split from BL-563 because it lands in a different layer and is a FORWARD constraint, not a bug fix. Era -1 already obeys it (history_sim.cpp:1019, 'TERRITORY MOVES AT PROVINCE GRANULARITY, NEVER TILE'), so the ruling confirms existing behaviour there. Campaign-era conquest DOES NOT EXIST - MILITARY.md lists 'any consequence to holding the field' as absent - so this is a constraint on unbuilt work, and it collides with BL-518's arrangement that provinces are generation output fixed at campaign start and excluded from state_hash for that reason. The reconciling reading: the PARTITION stays fixed, OWNERSHIP of a province moves.
items.design:
## Ben, 2026-08-22 (elicitation form, second half of the BL-563 answer)

> "have it be impossible to conquer a tile without also controlling the province"

Split from BL-563 rather than carried inside it: that item is a generation bug in
`province.cpp`, this is a rule about how territory changes hands, in different files
and a different layer. Recorded in **NR-560**.

## Era -1 already obeys this. The ruling confirms it.

`history_sim.cpp:1019` carries the invariant in capitals already:

> TERRITORY MOVES AT PROVINCE GRANULARITY, NEVER TILE.

with BL-308's ground-down-frontier mechanism underneath it (the bar a victory must
clear falls as accumulated contest rises, because a flat threshold meant battles
outnumbered conquests by up to 1000:1). So for the generation sim this item asserts
existing behaviour and should be verified, not built.

## Campaign-era conquest does not exist, so this is a constraint on unbuilt work

`MILITARY.md`'s explicit *what is absent* list names **"any consequence to holding
the field"**. BL-467/468/469 landed the engagement trigger, the battle card and the
dispatch stream on 2026-08-21 — a fight is now a thing in the world — but winning one
takes no ground. There is nothing today that this rule would constrain.

That makes the item's real content a **forward invariant**: whatever eventually gives
a battle a territorial consequence must move a whole province, never a tile.

## The architectural collision, which is the reason this needs design before build

**BL-518 states the opposite arrangement, deliberately and with its reasoning
attached.** Ben ruled there that borders move **during generation only**, fixed once
the campaign starts — and `world.hpp:250` documents the consequence: `provinces` is
excluded from `state_hash` *because* "the partition is generation output and never
moves once built, so including it would make every tick hash carry a constant". BL-518
then warns in as many words:

> "If this item ever grew into campaign-era border changes, that whole arrangement
> would need revisiting."

This is that growth. Two things now need separating, and conflating them is the
expensive mistake:

**(1) The PARTITION** — which tiles compose province P. **(2) The OWNERSHIP** — which
nation holds P.

The reconciling reading, and the recommendation: **the partition stays fixed
generation output; only ownership moves.** Conquest transfers a province wholesale
from one nation to another without redrawing a single edge. That satisfies Ben's rule
exactly (a tile cannot change hands alone, because tiles are not what changes hands),
and it leaves `world::provinces` immutable, still outside `state_hash`, still checked
by `determinism_harness` across two generations, and still safe as a BL-467 battle-seed
input — a partition that moved mid-campaign would silently move battle outcomes.

What *does* become live tick-mutable state under that reading is the nation-to-tile
relation. `nation_component::tiles` is documented as "populated by Pass 2 (territory
expansion) and **stable thereafter**", which stops being true. That field, or whatever
replaces it, then has to enter `state_hash` and the BL-536 save format — and the
BL-536 design is being written now, which is why this is worth settling early rather
than late.

## Open, and genuinely undecided

- **Does the recommendation hold?** Fixed partition + mobile ownership is the cheap,
  coherent answer, but it means a conquered province keeps a shape drawn for a nation
  that no longer holds it. Whether that reads as history or as an artifact is a
  judgement call.
- **What triggers a transfer?** `resolve_campaign_battle` returns an outcome; nothing
  consumes it territorially. Era -1 uses an accumulating contest bar (BL-308) rather
  than a single decisive battle, and that mechanism is measured and works — reusing
  its shape at campaign grain is the obvious first candidate.
- **What happens to buildings and units on transferred ground?** A province changing
  hands with a rival's extractors standing on it is an economy question, not a
  military one, and BL-225 (seizure sentiment/credit cost) is the nearest existing
  design.
- **Does `nation_component::resource_abundance` recompute?** It is documented as
  computed in Pass 3 over owned tiles. If ownership moves, it is stale.

## Sequencing

Requires **BL-563**. A conquest rule at province grain is incoherent while a province
can span two nations — "control the province" has no single answer when two nations
already hold parts of it.
